utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Good morning to the technical booth; good morning interpreters, legal assistants, registry; good morning counsel for the Prosecution. I see that Ms. Hollis is with us today. Good morning counsel for the Defence. It seems that they are all here. And finally, good morning to the accused. The Prosecutor has proposed that the examination of Witness A be held in -- under special circumstances. The Prosecutor emphasised that the witness in question has already testified in a previous case, and that the contents of her testimony are particularly traumatising. The risk involved would therefore be that of another victimisation of the witness by making her remember painful events without at the same time special interests for the Defence. The Defence has already received the previous statement of the witness, and it seems that this particular statement would not be to any interest of the Judges as well. The Chamber is fully aware of the risk of a second victimisation or a secondary victimisation in this case. It is possible that this be a tertiary victimisation. Clearly Witness A is a very important witness, both for the Prosecution and for the Defence, and it seems that it is of a special interest for one particular accused. The Chamber has already taken account of the special situation of this witness who is coming to testify once again by granting a very high level of protection; however, in this case, it seems important that both the Prosecution and the Defence can proceed with the examination-in-chief and cross-examination of the witness in such a way as they are able to properly present their arguments before the Chamber. However, the Chamber wishes to note that persons who have suffered such painful events are especially vulnerable. The Chamber wishes to appeal to the parties not to ask questions which are unnecessary, and that the question be -- questions be asked in such a way that is fully appropriate in respect of the circumstances. The Chamber wishes to thank the parties in advance, and decides to follow the procedure which has so far been applied, that is, the usual procedure. This has been the ruling of the Chamber. I think that we can now proceed with a new witness. Ms. Hollis.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, the Prosecution would call Witness F, and this witness's testimony will be heard in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would note as this witness is brought into the courtroom, that if Your Honours have no objection, the witness is here with a support person. The witness has requested that the support person be allowed to listen to the testimony for any purposes of support. This individual is also the witness's therapist. We have asked the defence if it is permissible that the support person sit in the technical booth and listen to the evidence. The Defence has indicated they have no objection to this. So if Your Honours have no objection, we would ask leave for the support person to sit in the technical booth during Witness F's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is the response of the Defence, please? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, good morning. We are somewhat confused because the information we received was that it was the lawyer of Witness F, and we agreed to that, but this has caused a bit of a confusion with us. It is not very important, we still agree to that, but we would like to know who the individual in question really is, if that is the lawyer or a therapist.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Well, I'm confused as well, Your Honours, because certainly we would never have said it's the lawyer. This lady is a therapist. She's not a lawyer. As far as I understand, this witness doesn't have a lawyer. So it is the therapist that we're talking about who would sit in, and it is for purposes of therapy should this testimony traumatise the victim. And our understanding was the Defence had no objection, so I apologise for any confusion. Perhaps we've had some problem in communication because of the language, Your Honour. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] That is a possibility as well, Your Honour. We would interpret it as counsel, but we do not object to the application made by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am also a bit confused because I first of all did not order for the blinds to be lowered, and I didn't say that we had to go into private session as early as this, and apparently there is a very serious problem here, and we should have a five-minute break. Let me add that I was aware of the fact that a psychiatrist would be in the courtroom in order to help the witness if it is necessary. We all understand, I hope, that this is a very delicate situation, and the Chamber was already informed of the matter. However, we need to have at least a five-minute break at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In view of the request of the Prosecutor to have a psychiatrist present who is treating the witness, and the non-objection of the Defence, the Chamber decides to authorise the presence of this professional person in the technical booth, but on condition that this therapist signs a statement committing herself not to reveal any information from these hearings because they're being held under conditions of confidentiality. Therefore, she is obliged -- she has to pledge in writing not to speak to anyone about these things outside her professional therapeutic treatment of the witness. So understand those conditions, the Chamber does authorise the presence of this person. We are now going to go into closed session and have the witness brought in. Mr. Usher, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: be reconvened on Thursday the 14th day of September, 2000, at 9.30 a.m.
